Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8547-retire-dead-engine-strings`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and ⛔ never writes the assignee field.

## Why this one is dispatched when several p2s beside it are not

This card is **determinate**: the direction is settled, the scope is eight lines, and the instrument that established the four zeros already ran with a lit control. Most of the `pm:queue` p2 backlog I read today turned out to be **ruling-shaped** — objectui#8449, objectui#8429, objectui#8513 all say in their own bodies that picking a direction is a maintainer's call. This one says the opposite: *"deleting them is a separate call. This card is that call."*

## ⭐ The precondition is the whole job — do it before you delete anything

The card's own instruction, and I am making it a gate:

> ⚠️ Before deleting, re-run the four reproductions **plus the lit control** on the current tree. A key that has gained a reader since `34c22ad39` must not be deleted, and the control is what proves the re-run reached the corpus.

⇒ **Four zeros, plus one non-zero.** Report all five outputs verbatim.

```
git grep -n 'engine.directory.allPackages'   -- packages apps examples e2e content docs scripts
git grep -n 'engine.directory.packageFilter' -- packages apps examples e2e content docs scripts
git grep -n 'engine.list.allPackages'        -- packages apps examples e2e content docs scripts
git grep -n 'engine.list.packageFilter'      -- packages apps examples e2e content docs scripts
git grep -n 'engine.directory.quickFind'     -- packages apps          ← the LIT CONTROL
```

The control must return `DirectoryPage.tsx`, `StudioHomePage.tsx` and the two `i18n.ts` definition lines. **If it does not fire, your corpus is wrong and the four zeros mean nothing** — stop and report rather than deleting on a broken instrument.

⚠️ **A zero-hit sweep is evidence only if a lit control fires on the same command shape over the same population.** That sentence is why this card exists in a deletable state at all; do not skip the half that earns it.

⚠️ Two traps in the command shape itself, both measured in this repo:
- `git grep -- 'packages/*/src'` matches **nothing** (0 files vs 2691 for `'packages/*/src/*'`). The card's `-- packages apps …` form is the *directory* form and is correct — ⛔ do not "improve" it into a glob.
- `git grep -c` counts **LINES, not entries.** Use `-n` and read the hits.

## Scope — eight lines, and the fences are hard

- ✅ Delete the four keys from **both** `ENGINE_STRINGS_EN` and `ENGINE_STRINGS_ZH` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`.
- ⛔ **Do not touch any other key in that table.** The other 1489 keys' retirement is objectui#8388 and is a different kind of work.
- ⛔ **Do not add a gate here.** That is objectui#8388's deliverable, explicitly.
- ⚠️ Line numbers (`197 / 198 / 252 / 254` en, `2136 / 2137 / 2191 / 2192` zh) are from `34c22ad39` and **will have drifted**. Re-locate every one by content. I read four PM-supplied line numbers off a stale working tree earlier today and nearly "corrected" a dev who was right — the addresses are never the fact.

## ⚠️ One live collision the card cannot know about

**PR #8675 is open and armed on `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`** — objectui#8057's server-refusal gate adds keys to that same file. Different region, so git should merge it cleanly, but:

- check whether #8675 has landed before you branch, and
- if it lands while you are working, **merge `main` in** (⛔ never rebase or force-push) and re-run the five greps afterwards, because a merge can bring in a new reader.

## Verification

- The deletion's own evidence is the five grep readings. Beyond that: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` from the **repo root with paths**, and the i18n gates (`check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`) — each must print its **own verdict line**, ⛔ not merely exit 0.
- ⚠️ `check:doc-snippets` / `check:readme-exports` / `check:eager-closure` and `type-check` all fail on an **unbuilt tree** (`TS2307` for every workspace import). That is a **precondition**, recorded as **NOT MEASURED** — build the dependency closure first if you want a real reading.
- ⚠️ **An assertion never observed to fail has not been tested.** If you add or adjust any pin here, it must be observed red. If the honest answer is "this deletion needs no new pin because the keys had no readers", **say that** rather than manufacturing one — a pin over a key nobody reads is the same defect as the key.
- ⛔ `--no-inline-config` is an **objectstack** convention and manufactures objectui errors CI does not have. Run vitest from the repo root with paths; `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE` is refused by guard objectui#3378, and `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently re-roots onto `apps/console`.
- `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**; the real exemption is an **empty-frontmatter** changeset. `@object-ui/app-shell` publishes, so decide on the evidence rather than the label.

## Deliverables

Worktree → verify the five greps → delete → changeset → push → **draft** PR. Return the structured JSON `os-dev-report` to the PM **and** post it as a comment here. Every GitHub comment ends with:

```
```

⛔ Never put a model identifier in a commit message, PR title/body, code comment, or any pushed artifact. Commit messages end with:
```
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S
```

Small card, but the precondition is not a formality: **a key that gained a reader since the measurement must not be deleted**, and only the re-run can tell you.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8687 is out of draft and armed.

Eight deletions, no insertions, no other key touched. Small card, and three things in the execution are worth keeping.

## ⭐ The lit control's own address moved — which is the card's point, demonstrated on itself

> lit control … 4 hits (`DirectoryPage.tsx:256`, `StudioHomePage.tsx:274`, `i18n.ts:187`, `i18n.ts:2123` — **the zh address moved from 2126, which is exactly why nothing here reads a line number**).

The card's table said `2136 / 2137 / 2191 / 2192` for the zh block, measured on `34c22ad39`. Every one of them had drifted, **including the control's own**. The deletion was done **by matching the two-space-indented key literal, never by line address**, with the removal count asserted (8) and the file's line total checked either side (4700 → 4692).

I read four PM-supplied line numbers off a stale working tree earlier today and nearly used them to "correct" a dev who was right. Same lesson, second demonstration in one session.

## ⭐ The mid-flight collision was handled the way the dispatch asked

I warned that **PR #8675 was open on the same file**. It **landed mid-flight** (`9073cf018`). The response:

> main was merged in twice (#8673, then #8675 — **merge, never rebase, never force-push**) and **all five greps were re-run after each merge**: four zeros, control still firing, and neither landed range mentions any of the four names.

⇒ the precondition was treated as **re-checkable state, not a one-time gate.** That is the whole risk of this card — *a key that has gained a reader since the measurement must not be deleted* — and a merge is precisely the event that could introduce one. #8675's `+2` keys and this card's `-8` merged cleanly in different regions, as predicted.

## ⭐ No pin was manufactured, and the reason was stated

> **NO NEW PIN**, stated rather than manufactured: these keys had no readers, and **a pin over a key nobody reads is the same defect as the key**; no gate added either (objectui#8388's deliverable).

I asked for exactly this and it is the easy place to pad a PR. The deletion's entire evidence is the five grep readings, and the report says so — no ablation, because nothing was added that could be observed red. ⛔ The gate fence held too.

## ⚠️ One honest negative worth carrying upstream

> **NOTE both i18n gates are structurally blind to this table** (the call-site gate classifies it "module-local table" by declaration, the drift gate reads only the ten packs) — **recorded, not claimed as coverage.**

Both gates exit 0 with real verdict lines (`check:i18n-keys`: *"Every in-scope call-site key resolves against the en pack (2976 keys)"*; `check:i18n-drift`: *"0 en value(s) changed"*) — and **neither of those verdicts is about this table.** Quoting the verdict and then saying it does not cover the change is the opposite of the usual failure, where a green gate is offered as evidence for something it never measured.

⇒ that is direct evidence for **objectui#8388**, whose deliverable is the retirement instrument for the other 1489 keys: the two gates that look like they would catch a dead key here **cannot see this table at all.** I am noting it there.

The changeset is empty-frontmatter and justified on evidence rather than on the label: `app-shell` publishes, but `t()` is not exported from the package entry and the exports map offers only `.` and `./styles.css`, so nothing a tarball consumer can reach changes.
